summary: The change adds versioned settlement accounting, signal-based death classification, infrastructure recovery, and inert dry-run guards. The biggest risk is that legacy ledgers are warned about but their lifetime infrastructure counter is reused as a consecutive gate, causing valid resumed routes to be falsely reported incomplete.

findings.title: Epoch-1 infrastructure counts are reused as epoch-2 consecutive gates
findings.evidence: The loader says `st.attempts_infra_total = st.attempts_infra` and leaves the old value unchanged because `the gate value is whatever that older ledger recorded`; the new planner then gates on `infra_spent and infra_spent >= infra_budget`. In c67a955, `attempts_infra` was a lifetime count and was never cleared when a later attempt produced a record.
findings.why_wrong: For example, an epoch-1 ledger can contain a final retryable record with `attempts_record=1`, `attempts_infra=1`, `finished=false`, and `infra_budget=1` after an earlier failed launch and an interrupted forced rerun. The new planner sees record budget remaining but infra spent, returns unsettled `SKIP_EXHAUSTED`, and exits 1 without retrying. The warning does not correct the state, and the next save stamps epoch 2 so later resumes may stop warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Migrate epoch-1 ledgers explicitly, or keep them under legacy accounting until a safe migration is performed. Do not reuse the old lifetime counter as the new streak; preserve it only as the total and establish a separately justified current streak before applying the new gate.

findings.title: Dry-run still mutates a corrupt ledger by renaming it
findings.evidence: `main()` calls `RunState.load_or_create(...)` before any dry-run branch. On unreadable JSON, `load_or_create` executes `p.replace(backup)` and returns a fresh state. The dry-run fix only guards later `state.save()` calls.
findings.why_wrong: A dry run against a corrupt or temporarily unreadable ledger changes the durable output tree despite the documented claim that it writes nothing. The next real run sees no ledger, loses persisted counters and settlement state, and can rerun routes or produce a different completion/report outcome.
findings.suggested_fix: Make ledger loading read-only for dry-run: report the parse error in memory without renaming the file, or use a non-mutating preview loader.
